tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced an experimental vision model on Sep 1, then shipped V4.1-Flash on Sep 10 claiming it beats flagship V4-Pro while cutting the memory agents need to run it. The efficiency claim rattled Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron shares within a day, and DeepSeek quantified it Sep 13 as a 75% HBM and 87.5% SSD cut.
whats_new: DeepSeek is routing all V4-Pro API traffic to V4.1-Flash under the hood at Flash's lower rate, which itself dropped again Sep 14 to $0.003 per million cached input tokens.
why_it_matters: Anyone calling the V4-Pro endpoint is now served different weights than they pinned, at a price that keeps falling, without a version bump to signal either change.

status.detail: A Sep 1 vision precursor led to a Sep 10 launch beating V4-Pro on quality while cutting agent memory needs; the efficiency claim rattled memory-chip stocks by Sep 11, and by Sep 14 DeepSeek was routing all V4-Pro traffic to V4.1-Flash at a price that kept falling.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources an experimental vision model, V4-Flash-Vision-Exp
beats.summary: A native vision preview lands over a week before the full V4.1-Flash release; one outlet flags DeepSeek's benchmark claims as needing independent proof.

beats.headline: A two-day limited beta natively integrates multimodal capabilities
DeepSeek unveils V4.1-Flash, claims it beats flagship V4-Pro
beats.summary: The new model launches as an upgrade over DeepSeek's own current flagship.

beats.headline: Cuts agent memory needs and slashes agentic costs by 80%
Efficiency claim rattles Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron shares
beats.summary: Multiple outlets tie the memory-savings claim to a same-day dip in memory-chip stocks.

beats.headline: Pricing pressure builds as reviewers call the architecture a bigger leap than a point release
DeepSeek puts numbers on the memory cut: 75% less HBM, 87.5% less SSD
DeepSeek quietly swaps V4-Pro traffic for V4.1-Flash at Flash pricing
beats.summary: Four days after launch, calls to the V4-Pro endpoint are served by V4.1-Flash instead, billed at the cheaper Flash rate.

beats.headline: 552B-parameter spec surfaces as a community uncensored fine-tune racks up downloads
Cached-input pricing drops again to $0.003 per million tokens

open_questions: Does the claimed memory-footprint cut hold up in independent agent-workload benchmarks, not just DeepSeek's own numbers?
Will DeepSeek formally deprecate the V4-Pro endpoint, or keep serving V4.1-Flash under the old name indefinitely?
Do outputs from the V4-Pro endpoint show measurable quality or behavior differences now that V4.1-Flash serves them?
Was the Sep 1 vision-exp precursor's benchmark claim, which one outlet called unverified, ever independently confirmed?
take_for_builders: Re-run your eval suite against the V4-Pro endpoint: you're getting V4.1-Flash's outputs at a still-falling price, and any prompt or behavior tuned to V4-Pro specifically may have silently drifted.
